item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=meta-reasoning+mechanisms+epistemic+boundaries+large+language+models+unrecognized+failure+modes&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6641752\", \"title\": [\"Structural Simulation Benchmark for Reasoning Large Language Models: Accuracy, Reliability, and Failure Modes\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large language models (LLMs), particularly reasoning-oriented models optimized for long-horizon and multi-step inference, are increasingly used to assist programming and scientific research. However, their reliability in structural engineering computations—where validity is highly sensitive to implementation details—remains insufficiently quantified. This study evaluates four recent reasoning-oriented LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeekV3.2, GPT5, and Grok 4 Fastreasoning) under a unified API-based setup with default parameters and proposes a novel evaluation framework tailored for structural simulation. Five problems are designed to cover linear elasticity problems, forced vibration of a Timoshenko beam, and frame analysis. Solution strategies are constrained for comparability, and all generated codes are executed in a fixed Python environment with results verified against ABAQUS simulations or analytical solutions. The framework explicitly probes the importance of boundary conditions, selection of modeling assumptions, and implementation robustness. Common failure modes include incorrect treatment of traction-free boundaries, local-to-global transformation errors due to inconsistent local-axis definitions, and numerical instability induced by the choices of ways to impose boundary conditions. Overall reliability shows GPT‐5 is best model among those models tested. These findings suggest that verification-oriented workflows and automated consistency checks are essential for the safe use of LLM-assisted structural computation.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6641752\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.62891/45c2ef5a\", \"title\": [\"Arkhe(N): Design Fiction as a Structured Method for Probing Epistemic Boundaries in Large Language Models\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.62891/45c2ef5a\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 2, 17]]…
